:::{#exm-kernel-exponential}
#### The kernel, normalizing constant, and mode of an exponential density

The [exponential density](#def-exponential) with rate $\rate$ is $f(t) = \rate \ef{-\rate t}$ for $t \ge 0$.
Its [kernel](#def-kernel) is $g(t) = \ef{-\rate t}$ on $t \ge 0$,
and the [normalizing constant](#def-normalizing-constant) is

$$
\ba
c
&= \frac{1}{\int_0^{\infty} \ef{-\rate t}\,dt}
&& \text{(definition of the normalizing constant)} \\
&= \frac{1}{1/\rate}
&& \text{(integrate)} \\
&= \rate.
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

The kernel is largest at $t = 0$, so by @thm-kernel-same-mode the [mode](#def-mode) of $f$ is $0$.

:::
